content.value_statement: React interfaces often fail around loading, errors, and empty data. This skill provides practical patterns for predictable async UI states.
actual_capabilities: Guides loading indicator decisions when cached data exists.
Provides an error handling hierarchy and retry component pattern.
Shows button loading and disabled-state patterns for async actions.
Defines empty state rules and contextual examples.
Gives a form submission pattern with validation and mutation feedback.
Includes a checklist for UI states, data, and mutations.
limitations: Does not provide runnable React components or package code.
Does not cover styling systems, accessibility audits, or full design systems.
Uses generic examples that must be adapted to project libraries.
Does not verify application behavior through tests.

use_cases.title: Stabilize Async Screens
use_cases.description: Apply loading, error, empty, and success patterns to screens that fetch remote data.

use_cases.title: Review UI State Coverage
use_cases.description: Check pull requests for missing feedback, swallowed errors, or repeated action triggers.

use_cases.title: Define Product Interaction Rules
use_cases.description: Create consistent expectations for how forms, lists, and mutations behave under failure.

prompt_templates.title: Add Missing UI States
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a single component.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this React component and add clear loading, error, empty, and success states using the react-ui-patterns skill.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Refetch Behavior
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for data fetching UX.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use react-ui-patterns to revise this data screen so cached content stays visible during background refetches.

prompt_templates.title: Harden Form Submission
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for mutation and validation flow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply react-ui-patterns to this form so validation, submission loading, duplicate prevention, and error feedback are handled consistently.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Feature Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this React feature with react-ui-patterns and report missing states, risky async behavior, and recommended UI changes.

output_examples.input: A list page keeps showing a spinner during refetch.
output_examples.output: Keep the existing list visible during refetch. Use full loading only when no data exists, and show subtle progress for updates.

output_examples.input: A mutation logs errors but users see no feedback.
output_examples.output: Surface the failure through a toast or inline message. Provide retry guidance and keep the failed state visible.

output_examples.input: A submit button can be clicked multiple times.
output_examples.output: Disable the button while submitting. Show a loading state and prevent invalid submissions before calling the mutation.

best_practices: Show full loading states only when no useful data is available.
Pair every async action with user-visible success or failure feedback.
Disable repeated triggers while requests are in progress.
anti_patterns: Replacing cached content with spinners during background refetches.
Logging errors without showing users a recovery path.
Submitting forms while invalid or already loading.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps build React interfaces with clear loading, error, empty, button, and submission states.

faq.question: Does it include production components?
faq.answer: No. It provides patterns and examples that developers adapt to their component library.

faq.question: Can it help with cached data refetches?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends keeping existing data visible and using loading indicators only when no data is available.

faq.question: Does it cover form validation?
faq.answer: It covers validation gates, mutation loading, disabled submit buttons, and user-visible error feedback.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it replace accessibility testing?
faq.answer: No. Accessibility, keyboard behavior, and screen reader testing still need separate review.
